clinical_features.symptoms:
Clinical features of Acute Liver Failure 
 
History 
Clinical signs on examination of ALF 
► Date of onset of symptoms 
► Travel history 
► Drug use – prescription and illicit 
► Alcohol use 
► Herbal or traditional medication use 
► Target symptoms consistent with the 
presenting complication 
► Exposure to a viral illness (sexual contacts, 
body piercing) 
► Jaundice 
► RUQ tenderness 
► Hepatomegaly 
► Splenomegaly 
► Ascites 
► Evidence of bleeding 
► Evidence of infection 
► Asterixis (hepatic flap) 
► Evidence of encephalopathy 
 
Grading of Hepatic Encephalopathy (HE) 
 
Grade 
Intellectual Function 
Neuromuscular Function 
I 
Impaired attention, irritable, depressed, personality 
changes 
Tremor, apraxia, incoordination 
II 
Drowsy, poor memory, behavioural changes, sleep 
disturbances 
Asterixis, ataxia, slow slurred 
speech 
III 
Confusion, somnolence, disorientation, amnesia 
Hypoactive reflexes, clonus, 
nystagmus, muscle rigidity 
IV 
Stupor, coma 
Dilated pupils, decerebrate 
posture, oculocephalic reflex

warnings:
Note: 
Observe for vomiting for 1 hour in the ED. If no vomiting ➔ discharge 
If vomiting occurs within 1 hour, re-administer dose & observe. 
If vomiting persists ➔ Refer to Internal Medicine 
SIGNS & SYMPTOMS 
* Fever 
* Arthralgia 
* Fatigue 
* Myalgia 
* Malaise 
* Abdominal pain 
* Anorexia 
* Vomiting 
* Headache 
* Dizziness 
* Cough  
        * Rigors 
* Travel history 
 
HIGH RISK GROUPS 
* Children 
* Pregnant & postpartum 
* Elderly > 65 years 
* HIV 
* Previous splenectomy 
* Travel
record.disposition:
Disposition 
• ALL patients with ALF should be referred to a physician for further management. 
• If intubated – admit/transfer to ICU 
• Early consultation with Liver Transplant specialists
